source.observation: A millwright was replacing the coupling guard on the number 2 pump drive with the pump control switch in the OFF position at the local panel. The pump discharge line was still pressurized at the isolation valve, and the millwright had both hands inside the coupling housing while I observed.

decisionCriticalGaps.description: whether the pump drive was locked and tagged at its disconnect and the discharge line bled down, or whether the local OFF switch is the only isolation applied

truth.authoringRationale: A stated pressurized line with hands inside the housing establishes a present stored-energy condition. What is open is which CONTROL was applied, not whether a hazard exists, which is the exact pair the v7 definitions decide explicitly. Lockout is defensible rather than present because the text establishes servicing without establishing that isolation is absent. No family is forbidden here: every one of the four is at least arguable from the stated facts.

evidence.quotedText: with the pump control switch in the OFF position at the local panel

expertHazardCandidates.evidenceBasis: The pump was only turned off at a local control switch, not physically isolated with lockout/tagout devices, while the millwright performed work with hands inside the coupling housing.
expertHazardCandidates.reasoning: Placing a control switch in the OFF position at a local panel is not equivalent to lockout/tagout isolation; the drive could be re-energized by others or by an automatic/remote control action while the millwright's hands are inside the coupling housing, exposing him to unexpected startup or rotating equipment contact.

evidence.quotedText: The pump discharge line was still pressurized at the isolation valve

expertHazardCandidates.evidenceBasis: The discharge line is stated as currently pressurized while work is being performed on the pump drive coupling.
expertHazardCandidates.reasoning: Residual pressure in the discharge line at the isolation valve is a current stored-energy hazard; if the line, seals, or associated fittings were to fail or be disturbed during the coupling guard work, pressurized fluid release could occur, and this energy has not been relieved or verified at zero.

decisionCriticalClarifications.question: Was the pump drive physically isolated (e.g., breaker locked out, energy source de-energized and verified) beyond placing the local control switch in the OFF position, or is the OFF switch the only isolation in place?
decisionCriticalClarifications.whyItMatters: If the drive was locked out at the energy source with the switch OFF as one part of a full isolation, the exposure to unexpected re-energization is controlled; if the OFF switch at the local panel is the sole control with no lockout device applied, the millwright's hands inside the coupling housing are exposed to a real risk of unexpected startup. These two answers lead to different conclusions about whether the current work method is acceptable or must stop immediately.
decisionCriticalClarifications.evidenceGap: Whether lockout/tagout devices (not just a local switch) were applied to the pump drive's energy source before the millwright placed his hands inside the coupling housing.

crossHazardInsights.reasoning: The pump drive lacks confirmed physical lockout (only a local switch is OFF) while the discharge line remains pressurized; if the incomplete electrical isolation allows unexpected motor start, the rotating coupling could also interact with or amplify the effects of the pressurized line, and the combination of an ungrounded electrical isolation with unrelieved stored hydraulic energy means two independent unresolved energy sources threaten the same worker with hands inside the housing, compounding the consequence of either single failure.

expertExplanation.summary: Beyond the identified machine guarding hazard, the millwright worked with both hands inside the coupling housing while the pump was isolated only by a local control switch in the OFF position rather than a verified lockout, and the discharge line remained pressurized — two separate unresolved energy sources (electrical/mechanical and hydraulic) present at the same point of exposure. expertHazardCandidates.evidenceBasis: A below-grade concrete vault with a restricted 24-inch opening and no continuous forced ventilation was entered with no atmospheric testing performed beforehand, meaning the atmosphere is unverified at time of entry.
expertHazardCandidates.reasoning: Below-grade vaults with limited openings and no ventilation can accumulate hazardous or oxygen-deficient atmospheres. evidence.quotedText: no attendant was posted at the opening

expertHazardCandidates.evidenceBasis: No attendant was posted at the vault opening while two employees were inside performing work.

A short task with a fit-tested P100 is a different current decision from a multi-hour one, which requires engineering control and an exposure assessment now.

evidence.quotedText: inside an enclosed stairwell

expertHazardCandidates.evidenceBasis: The enclosed stairwell restricts natural dilution ventilation, worsening the airborne dust concentration and increasing exposure and cartridge loading beyond what the respirator alone addresses.
